newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank sees no change in crown fixing band.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank sees no change in crown fixing band.

text.p: A change in the Czech crown's +/-7.5 percent daily fluctutation band is not imminent, Czech National Bank (CNB) Vice-governor Jan Vit told Reuters on Tuesday.

"We think that the current fluctuation band is good enough for the present stage of economic development," Vit said. When asked if he saw any change to the band in the near future, Vit answered: "No."
The central bank fixes the crown daily within a +/-7.5 percent fluctuation band of its dollar/mark basket midpoint.

Foreign exchange dealers have said the market is wary of a change in the exchange rate regime, as a central bank method of adding more currency risk to the crown in an attempt to scare off inflows of speculative capital.

Last week, the government outlined a package of measures designed to kick-start the economy, and it was widely believed that the central bank would follow suit by easing monetary policy or by moving to allow the crown to depreciate to help lacklustre exports.

Speaking in the city of Brno at the opening of the FIBEX banking and finance exhibition, Vit reiterated the central bank's stance that inflation and stability in monetary policy were still its foremost concern.
"Our main aim is still to maintain monetary stability," he said.
"Within this... we have certain space on how to support policy which is oriented to reducing the balance of payments deficit and keep our main aim to minimise inflation," he added.
